candidate_updates.name: project-level lineage graph plus bounded dependency/ownership/evaluation task contracts

primary_evidence.result: Project2Task's routing ablation holds the downstream pipeline fixed and forces the router to use the second-ranked decomposition strategy. The graph-selected route averages 7.15 portfolio quality versus 6.48 for the runner-up, wins 9/10 project briefs, and shows the largest dimension gains in Task Division (+1.04), Overlap Control (+0.56), and Consistency (+0.62), with means/SD over five repeated evaluations.

candidate_updates.causal_refinement: Within this manuscript-based portfolio-scoring protocol, route choice is directly isolated from the downstream contract implementation because all other pipeline components are held identical. This upgrades the previously secondary-extracted 7.15-versus-6.48 result to primary-verified component evidence.
candidate_updates.downstream_bundle_boundary: The separate AutoResearchClaw result, task accuracy 0.536 to 0.759 and 0.766 to 0.830 after excluding invalid-execution zeros, still bundles route selection with generated structured contracts rather than isolating the router. One task decreases from 0.747 to 0.542, so structural guidance can overconstrain or misalign a task.
candidate_updates.remaining_boundary: Only ten project briefs/~30 tasks; portfolio quality is manuscript-based evaluation. The study does not isolate lineage-graph representation from the router objective itself, nor router effects from contract-content/repair effects in the downstream execution result.

candidate_updates.name: dual-channel persistent implementation contract across generation and repair

primary_evidence.setting: PaperBench Code-Dev, Gemini-3-Flash, 20 papers; stage-review repair capped at three attempts and repository-level repair at five rounds for full and ablation settings; all other components and repair budgets held fixed.
primary_evidence.result: Full persistent contract mean 39.7 (median 41.8); removing reference evidence falls to 21.6 (median 21.4, -18.1 mean), while removing implementation requirements falls to 25.6 (median 24.6, -14.1 mean). The full condition beats both channel ablations on all 20 targets.

candidate_updates.mechanism: Convert explicit paper requirements into stable source-anchored code obligations and separately bind implicit implementation/protocol evidence from related repositories; project both into work-package/file contracts that remain addressable during generation, validation, and targeted repair.
candidate_updates.causal_boundary: Strong same-backbone component evidence for paper-to-code scientific reproduction, but one run per paper-setting pair and a benchmark judge score; it does not establish open-ended scientific-discovery quality, claim validity, or a critique-only versus mandatory-repair causal effect.

matched_intervention_search.result: No fully matched open-ended science-domain same-model/tools/budget comparison isolating optional critique from mandatory evidence-changing repair, material claim downgrade, or hard block was identified in this pass.
nearby_evidence: Sibyl-AutoResearch exposes trial-to-behavior conversion and a failure registry but explicitly does not claim comparative performance from its traces.
OmniScientist implements deterministic research gates and reports gate-triggered rejections, but does not provide a clean no-gate same-budget causal arm for those gates.

ReproAgent supplies strong same-backbone contract-channel ablations for scientific paper-to-code reproduction, but its intervention targets specification preservation rather than optional critique versus mandatory epistemic repair.
